What it is

A diner, a mug wall and a gift shelf.

Charlie's is a small-town cafe on Roosevelt Avenue, a block off Highway 410 where the road heads east toward the White River and Sunrise.

Breakfast, from six

Country fried steak with sausage gravy, plate-sized buttermilk cakes, homemade hashbrowns and bacon that people write reviews about.

Lunch, from eleven

Quarter-pound burgers, the Mt. Rainier Reuben, fish and chips off home-cut fries — and a different soup for every weekday.

On the way to the mountain

People stop in on the drive out to Mount Rainier and say so in the reviews — brunch in Enumclaw, then the White River road.

A shelf of local goods

Sweatshirts, hanging fused-glass stars, homemade candles and custom cribbage boards, sold right off the window ledge.

Dine inTakeoutOrder online

The cafe

Everybody's mug is on the wall.

The banner strung across the side of the building says fifty years in business, family owned and operated for three generations.

Inside it's cedar plank walls and an oak counter, a Coca-Cola cruiser bike hung off the rafters, an old Coke serving tray by the door, and rows of regulars' personal coffee mugs racked behind the till. One reviewer wrote that the decor is "everything Coca-Cola." Another said the rustic log-cabin feel makes you feel like a local or a logger stopping in before work.

It's also a stop on the way to the mountain. Charlie's sits on Roosevelt Avenue where Highway 410 runs east out of Enumclaw, and the reviews read like it — families brunching here on their way out to Mount Rainier, then getting back on the road.

Find us

Roosevelt Avenue, a block off 410.

  1. Just walk in

    There's no reservation list. Take a booth or a stool at the counter.

  2. Or order ahead

    Their online ordering runs through Clover, and delivery through DoorDash.

  3. Bringing a crowd?

    Call first so they can set the tables. An 18% service charge applies to large groups.
